SOAI: AI tools could be used to sift through and detect problematic answers. As Stack Overflow ages, there is a large repository of obsolete or incorrect information. AI tools could scan through and detect ones that need updating. This does not address how to deal with them, but detection only. I find myself as a Stack Overflow user many times looking first at the question/answer date to filter whether I want to put in the effort to read it. AI tools could also be used to give suggestions to other questions/answers that might answer the current question. I am against allowing AI-based questions or answers. In fact, I support using AI to detect and flag questions / answers that may be AI generated. If some threshold is met, the answer may be invalidated and user penalized. I don't support it because it devalues the point system and social aspect of Stack Overflow that has made it so successful. If AI becomes a large fraction of the answers, people might view Stack Overflow more and more as a lesser version of actual AI tools like ChatGPT. The problem could compound itself because AI tools use sites like Stack Overflow as sources of information.

This could reduce the frustration of questions going unanswered due to poor titling or tagging.  Recommending related questions: When users are browsing questions, AI could recommend other relevant questions and answers based on similarity. This could help users find information faster and foster more connections between related topics.  Identifying low-quality or spam content: AI could flag suspicious posts, like spam or low effort questions and answers, for moderator review. This could help maintain a higher level of quality and usefulness on the platform.  Summarizing long or complex answers: For very long or highly technical answers, AI could generate a quick summary to help readers determine if they want to dive into the full details. This may encourage users to share their in-depth knowledge if they know it can still be accessed efficiently.  Moderating offensive comments: AI could detect inappropriate or harmful comments for moderator removal. No one should have to deal with toxic behavior while trying to share or access knowledge on Stack Overflow.  Overall, I believe using AI to handle repetitive, low-level tasks like titling, tagging, summarizing and moderating content could significantly improve the Stack Overflow user experience by allowing members and moderators to focus on more meaningful interactions and contributions. Of course, human judgment and oversight would still be essential to guide AI systems and ensure optimal performance. But on the whole, a well-designed balance of artificial and human intelligence could take Stack Overflow to the next level.
